etymology: From the medieval castle: a modest motte that is easy to defend, and a rich bailey that is not.
committed_when: The strong version of a claim has just been contested.
tell: The position shrinks under pressure and grows again in the next conversation.
counter: Name both claims and ask which one is being defended. Accepting the motte does not concede the bailey.
senses: Advancing a strong, controversial claim, then retreating to a modest, uncontroversial one when challenged - and re-advancing the strong claim once the pressure is off.
It works because the two claims are related. The retreat is sincere-sounding because the modest claim is genuinely held; the strong claim is never withdrawn, only set down.
example: *"Defund the police"* argued, then "we only mean reallocating the overtime budget" defended, then argued again by Thursday.

confused_with.tell: The motte switches between two claims; equivocation switches between two meanings of one word.
